property_summary: Transferring ownership should only succeed when called by the current owner; the bug allows any caller to change the owner, so after a call by a non-owner the owner remains unchanged in the reference but changes in the mutant.
After a non-owner calls transferOwnership, the owner state in the reference contract must remain unchanged, but the buggy contract allows an arbitrary caller to overwrite the owner.
For any caller, after transferOwnership is invoked, the owner is the new owner if and only if the caller was the previous owner; the bug allows any caller to change the owner.
For any caller that is not the current owner, a call to transferOwnership must revert; the bug lets a non-owner change the owner successfully.

For any caller, a call to transferOwnership must either revert (if not owner) or succeed (if owner); the bug allows any caller to succeed without reverting, making the revert status of the call the distinguishing property.
Only the current owner can change the owner, so a successful call to transferOwnership by a non-owner should not alter the stored owner address; the buggy version allows anyone to change it.

After any call to transferOwnership(newOwner) by the current owner, the stored owner must equal newOwner; the buggy modifier allow any caller to change it, so for a call by the owner, a concurrent attack by a non-owner in the same transaction could overwrite the owner to a different value, violating the property that the owner's final state matches the passed newOwner.

A successful transferOwnership call from any sender should leave the owner unchanged unless the sender is the current owner; the buggy modifier lets a non-owner change the owner to an arbitrary address.
After any non-reverting call to transferOwnership, owner() must equal the address argument that was passed; the bug version always sets owner to address(0x0) instead.

After a non-reverting call to transferOwnership from a recognized non-zero owner, the owner() must equal the passed argument and never be a specific burned address (0x0) when a non-zero address was passed; the bug always sets owner to 0x0 regardless.
For any caller that is the current owner, after a non-reverting call to transferOwnership(anyAddress), the new owner() must return that anyAddress; the bug always sets owner to address(0x0).
After the current owner non-revertingly calls transferOwnership, the stored owner must equal the passed argument; the bug always sets owner to address(0x0) even when the caller is the current owner.
For any caller that is the current owner, after a non-reverting call to transferOwnership(newOwner), the stored owner must equal newOwner; the bug always sets owner to address(0x0).
Only the current owner can change the owner; the bug allows any non‑owner to successfully call transferOwnership.

Calling transferOwnership(newOwner) as the current owner must update `owner` to `newOwner`; the bug never updates `owner`, so after a successful call, the bug leaves `owner` unchanged while the reference updates it.
After transferOwnership, the owner must equal the newOwner for any caller that is the current owner; the bug fails this because it never assigns the newOwner.
For any caller (including non-owners), a call to `owned()` should revert if `msg.sender` is not the owner; the mutant passes for all callers, violating the onlyOwner guard.
owned() should succeed when called by the owner, but the buggy modifier's require(false) makes it always revert, so the owner can never successfully call owned().
For any caller that is not the owner, the reference C allows owned() to succeed (the modifier only enforces msg.sender == owner), but the buggy version always reverts regardless of caller.
After a call to owned(), if the caller was the contract owner, the reference succeeds (returns), but the buggy version always reverts.

For any caller (including the zero address), a call to owned() succeeds in the reference contract if and only if the caller is the current owner; the buggy contract's always-reverting modifier breaks the "if" direction, causing it to revert even when called by the owner.

For any caller, after a call to owned() completes without reverting, the call must have been made by the contract owner; the buggy modifier always reverts, so it never completes, but the reference allows the owner to successfully call owned().
The modifier onlyOwner on owned() must restrict access; the bug removes it, allowing any caller to succeed instead of reverting.
After any call to transferOwnership(newOwner), the owner must equal newOwner; the bug leaves owner unchanged, violating this for any newOwner different from the current owner.
After a successful transferOwnership call, the owner must change to the new owner if the new owner is different from the current owner, which the bug violates by leaving the owner unchanged.
